parts.name: Nose cone
parts.what: Von Kármán (Haack) ogive, 300 mm long, with an 85 mm shoulder that slides into the upper tube.
parts.why: Cuts drag at the front of the rocket. Its shape barely changes apogee at Mach 0.4, so it was kept simple to print.
parts.how: The shoulder is a snug fit in the upper tube and is held with 2 small screws through the tube wall (suggested), so it can come off to reach the E-bay. It never separates in flight.

parts.name: Upper body tube (E-bay)
parts.what: 12.000 in body tube that holds the avionics bay.
parts.why: Keeps the electronics away from the ejection charge (they are on the other side of the bulkhead) and gives the BMP-280 still air to measure.
parts.how: Nose shoulder at the front; coupler 1 is epoxied into its aft end. Three Ø1/8 in static ports at station 16.54 in let outside pressure reach the BMP-280.

parts.name: Avionics sled (ESP-32 + BMP-280 + microSD)
parts.what: The flight computer: ESP-32 microcontroller, BMP-280 barometric altimeter, microSD logger, battery and an arming switch.
parts.why: Records the altitude the competition scores. The data must be handed in before leaving the launch site or the team is disqualified.
parts.how: Suggested mounting: the PLA sled rides on two threaded rods anchored in the bulkhead, so it can't slide during the ~13 g boost. Use a 9 V alkaline or metal-cased Li-ion battery, not a LiPo. The switch must be reachable from outside through a hole in the tube.

parts.name: Static ports (×3)
parts.what: Three Ø1/8 in holes drilled 120° apart through the upper tube, level with the avionics.
parts.why: The BMP-280 measures altitude from air pressure. Without vent holes the sealed E-bay keeps ground pressure and reads nothing useful.
parts.how: Drill them clean, away from the nose shoulder and joints. They are small enough not to weaken the tube.

parts.name: Ballast bay A
parts.what: Removable steel washers on the forward face of the bulkhead, inside coupler 1.
parts.why: Fine-tunes the apogee to the 2,000 ft target on launch day. Together with bay B the weight is split 69 : 31, so the CG (and stability) doesn't move.
parts.how: Washers on a bolt through the bulkhead with a lock nut. The bulkhead carries their inertia (≈13 g × 91 g ≈ 12 N), far below what 1/4 in birch can take.

parts.name: Coupler 1 — separation joint
parts.what: 4 in coupler: 2 in epoxied inside the upper tube, 2 in sliding into the middle tube.
parts.why: This is where the rocket splits open at ejection so the parachute can come out.
parts.how: Bonded to the upper tube. A snug friction fit (or 2 nylon shear pins) holds it in the middle tube until the ejection charge pressurises the bay. Pop-test it on the ground.

parts.name: Bulkhead
parts.what: Solid birch disk epoxied inside the aft end of coupler 1.
parts.why: Seals the front of the pressure vessel (so the ejection gas pushes the sections apart) and protects the electronics from the hot gas.
parts.how: Epoxy fillet all round on both faces. The forward U-bolt passes through it, so the opening shock of the parachute goes U-bolt → bulkhead → coupler → upper tube.

parts.name: U-bolt + quick link
parts.what: Steel U-bolt through the bulkhead with a quick link on it.
parts.why: The forward anchor of the shock cord and the attachment point for the parachute.
parts.how: Two nuts + washers on the forward face of the bulkhead. The quick link lets you unclip the recovery harness after a flight.

parts.name: Swivel
parts.what: Ball-bearing swivel between the U-bolt and the parachute.
parts.why: Stops the parachute lines twisting up as the rocket spins under canopy.
parts.how: Clipped to the U-bolt quick link; the parachute bridle clips to its other end.

parts.name: Middle body tube (recovery bay)
parts.what: 13.000 in body tube: the recovery bay.
parts.why: Holds the parachute, Nomex and shock cord. With the bulkhead in front and the motor's forward closure behind, it is the pressure vessel the ejection charge fills.
parts.how: Coupler 1 slides into its front (separation joint); coupler 2 is screwed into its back (access joint). The forward rail button is screwed through it 30 mm from its aft end.

parts.name: Parachute 42 in (packed)
parts.what: 42 in round ripstop parachute, folded and rolled.
parts.why: Brings the 1.25 kg (burnt-out) rocket down at about 17 ft/s so it lands relaunchable (worth 150 points).
parts.how: Bridle on the swivel near the forward U-bolt, so the nose section hangs from it and the fin can hangs below on the shock cord.

parts.name: Nomex blanket
parts.what: Flame-proof cloth wrapped around the packed parachute.
parts.why: The ejection charge fires from the motor end; the Nomex keeps the hot gas and particles from melting the chute.
parts.how: Burrito-wrap the chute so the open side faces forward; tie the Nomex to the shock cord so it doesn't fly away.

parts.name: Shock cord 15 ft (packed)
parts.what: 15 ft of Kevlar cord, Z-folded with masking-tape bundles.
parts.why: Keeps both halves tethered together after separation and absorbs the snatch load when the chute opens.
parts.how: Aft end: quick link on the I-hook on the forward centering ring. Forward end: the U-bolt quick link. The load path to the fin can is cord → I-hook → centering ring → motor tube & body tube.

parts.name: Coupler 2 — access joint
parts.what: 4 in coupler: 2 in epoxied into the fin can, 2 in into the middle tube.
parts.why: Lets you open the rocket just above the fin can to reach the I-hook, ballast bay B and the shock-cord attachment without cutting anything.
parts.how: Bonded to the lower tube and held in the middle tube with screws (it does NOT separate in flight). It sits 2.1 in above the forward centering ring, as the club recommends.

parts.name: Lower body tube (fin can)
parts.what: 11.000 in body tube carrying the motor mount and fins.
parts.why: The strongest, heaviest section: it takes the motor thrust and the fin loads.
parts.how: Three slots let the fin tabs pass through the wall to the motor tube. The aft rail button screws through the wall into a backing block, 20 mm from the aft end.

parts.name: I-hook + quick link
parts.what: Closed eye-bolt (I-hook) through the forward centering ring.
parts.why: The aft anchor of the shock cord.
parts.how: Nut + washer on each side of the centering ring, epoxied. The ring is bonded to both the motor tube and the body tube, so the load spreads into the whole fin can.

parts.name: Ballast bay B
parts.what: Removable washers on the forward face of the forward centering ring.
parts.why: The other 31 % of the launch-day ballast. Because it sits behind the CG and bay A sits in front, adding both in a 69 : 31 ratio keeps stability unchanged.
parts.how: Two bolts through the centering ring with lock nuts; reach them through coupler 2.

parts.name: Centering ring — forward
parts.what: Birch ring centring the motor tube at its front end.
parts.why: Holds the motor tube concentric and carries the I-hook load and ballast B.
parts.how: Epoxied to the motor tube and the body tube, with fillets on the forward face.

parts.name: Motor mount tube (29 mm)
parts.material: Cardboard, 31 mm OD / 29 mm ID, 9 in
parts.what: 9 in inner tube the 29 mm motor slides into.
parts.why: Transfers the motor's thrust into the airframe.
parts.how: Bonded to all three centering rings and to the fin tabs (through-the-wall), so thrust goes motor → retainer & thrust ring → motor tube → rings & fins → body tube.

parts.name: Centering ring — mid
parts.what: Ring just in front of the fin tabs.
parts.why: Supports the motor tube and gives the front of the fin tabs a hard stop.
parts.how: Epoxied to the motor tube and body tube; the fin tabs butt against its aft face.

parts.name: Fins ×3 (through-the-wall)
parts.what: Three trapezoidal fins at 120°: root 4.625 in, tip 4.000 in, span 3.75 in, sweep 0.50 in.
parts.why: Moves the centre of pressure aft to 37.21 in, giving 1.67–1.91 calibers of stability (club range 1.5–2.0). Flutter margin ≈1.9 (3/16 in birch).
parts.how: Each tab passes through a slot in the tube and is epoxied to the motor tube between the mid and aft centering rings, with fillets inside and outside. The tab, not the outer fillet, takes the landing loads.

parts.name: Epoxy fillets
parts.what: Rounded epoxy beads along both sides of each fin root.
parts.why: Spread the fin loads into the tube and smooth the airflow at the joint.
parts.how: Applied after the fins are tacked in; mask the tube for neat fillets.

parts.name: Centering ring — aft
parts.what: Ring 4 mm in from the aft end.
parts.why: Closes off the fin can and supports the rear of the motor tube and fin tabs.
parts.how: Epoxied to the motor tube and body tube; the motor retainer is bonded to the motor tube behind it.

parts.name: Motor retainer (29 mm)
parts.what: Threaded body epoxied to the motor tube plus a screw-on cap.
parts.why: Stops the motor sliding out of the back when the ejection charge fires.
parts.how: The body is JB-Weld/epoxied onto the motor tube end; the cap screws on over the motor's aft flange.

parts.name: Rail button — forward
parts.what: Rail guide that rides in the launch rail slot.
parts.why: Guides the rocket straight until it leaves the rail at ~66 ft/s (8 ft rail).
parts.how: Screw + nut through the tube wall with a backing plate. Swap to 1515 buttons if the pad uses 15/15 rail.

parts.name: Rail button — aft
parts.what: Second rail guide, 20 mm from the aft end, between two fins.
parts.why: Two buttons far apart keep the rocket aligned on the rail.
parts.how: Screw into a backing block glued inside the fin can between fins 2 and 3.

parts.name: Motor — AeroTech HP-H135W-14A
parts.what: H-class motor: 229 N·s total impulse, 116 N average thrust, ~2 s burn, White Lightning propellant.
parts.why: The team's chosen motor. Its delay is drilled from 14 s to 8 s so the ejection charge fires ~0.5 s before apogee.
parts.how: Slides into the motor tube; its aft thrust ring bears on the motor tube end and the retainer cap holds it in.
